commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor codebase to follow SE-EDU Java standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Java source code contains stylistic inconsistencies such as exposed
mutable fields in Task, non-standard boolean naming, redundant 'this'
qualifiers, unpunctuated Javadoc tags, and lines exceeding length limits.

Adhering to the SE-EDU Java Coding Standard and Google Java Style Guide
ensures proper OOP encapsulation, readability, and long-term
maintainability across the codebase.

Let's,
* enforce field encapsulation and class element ordering in Task
* rename boolean flags and methods to follow boolean naming rules
  (isRunning, isDone, isTaskMatchingDate)
* remove redundant 'this' keyword qualifiers across classes
* wrap lines exceeding character limits with continuation indentation
* standardize Javadoc tag punctuation and parameter naming
* update JUnit test cases to match the refactored method names

Applying predicate naming conventions and proper encapsulation prevents
unwanted field mutation while keeping all observable behavior identical.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add SE-EDU Java coding standard skill and mandate
commitResults.messageBody:
The project lacks an explicit skill and instruction mandating adherence
to the SE-EDU Java Coding Standard for coding agents.

Codifying SE-EDU Java conventions into a dedicated skill and referencing
it in the agent rules ensures automated tools and developers follow
consistent naming, formatting, and OOP standards.

Let's,
* create the seedu-java-coding-standard skill in .agents/skills/
* update AGENTS.md to mandate following the coding standard

Providing explicit rules prevents code quality degradation during
automated refactoring and feature implementation.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add SE-EDU Git conventions skill and mandate
commitResults.messageBody:
Git conventions for commit messages and branch naming in AGENTS.md are
only briefly summarized and lack a dedicated skill reference.

Providing a comprehensive skill ensures all future Git commits and branch
names strictly adhere to the structured SE-EDU Git guidelines.

Let's,
* create the seedu-git-standard skill in .agents/skills/
* update AGENTS.md to mandate adherence to seedu-git-standard

Having a structured template for commit messages ensures consistent,
informative version control history across all contributions.

The task manager has no way to search existing tasks by description,
which makes locating a task difficult as the list grows.

Let's add a case-insensitive find command that searches task descriptions,
handles invalid keywords, and displays matching tasks in insertion order.

Keeping search logic in TaskList and output formatting in Ui preserves the
existing separation of responsibilities and makes the behavior testable.

Add checkstyle and update files to comply with checkstyle
Refactor command handling and name text values
commitResults.messageBody:
Command dispatch mixes parsing with individual operations, while
messages and format strings are embedded throughout the application.
This makes the intent of the code harder to follow.

Extract command handlers and parsing helpers, and give text values
descriptive names across the application, storage, and task classes.
Add regression tests for argument extraction and mutation task counts
to help preserve behavior during the refactor.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix line breaks before console response dividers
commitResults.messageBody:
Responses without a trailing newline place the closing divider on the
same line as the response, making console output harder to read.

Terminate console responses and task list entries with a newline,
while preserving responses that already have one. Name the UI and
task list formatting values to make their purpose explicit.

Add tests for both response endings and update the UI test plan to
use Gradle so the build includes the JavaFX dependencies.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract stored task parsing into focused methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Task.fromFileString combines common storage validation, type selection,
field parsing, and completion restoration in one long method.
Understanding or changing one task format requires reading through the
validation paths for every other task type.

This method is used whenever saved tasks are loaded, so its complexity
makes persistence changes especially difficult to review. The course
code quality guidelines recommend avoiding long methods and separating
levels of abstraction.

Extract a small type dispatcher and private parsers for todos,
deadlines, and events. Keep common validation and completion restoration
in fromFileString so the loading sequence remains easy to follow. Use
private methods within Task to keep this refactoring focused without
introducing a new class or changing the public API.

Preserve field splitting, whitespace handling, validation order, error
messages, and completion status. Add seven regression tests for blank
fields, invalid event start dates, status error precedence, and
delimiters within todo descriptions. Existing tests cover valid task
types and their completion states.

Validate with Java 25: all 147 JUnit tests and all 13 exact-output UI
cases pass. Review the UI test plan and retain its expectations because
console behavior is unchanged.

Ui retains nine command-specific response methods even though James now
displays messages produced by CommandProcessor through showResponse.
Only unit tests call the old methods. Their message strings and task
formatting duplicate the active implementation.

These unused paths make it unclear where response changes belong and
allow tests to pass against code the application never uses. The course
code quality guidelines recommend deleting dead code and minimizing
duplication.

Remove the obsolete response methods and their unused constants and
imports. Keep Ui focused on console input, the greeting, and displaying
shared responses. Retain the existing CommandProcessor implementation so
this cleanup preserves application behavior.

Remove tests of the deleted methods and move their useful assertions to
the active command-processing path. Add exact-message tests for marking,
unmarking, keyword search, and date filtering, including empty results.
Strengthen existing list, error, and exit assertions while retaining
add/delete and console divider coverage.

Validate with Java 25: all 144 JUnit tests and all 13 exact-output UI
cases pass. Review the UI test plan and retain its expectations because
console behavior is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add undo for the last 20 task changes
commitResults.messageBody:
Task changes are saved immediately without a way to reverse mistakes.
Users need to recover deleted tasks and previous completion states.

Add session-only undo for successful changes, preserving task details
and order. Skip read-only commands, invalid input, and unchanged status
to keep undo focused on meaningful changes and avoid history conflicts.

Preserve tasks and undo history when saving fails. Restore console
line breaks to match the existing UI expectations, and document undo
behavior with unit tests and a complete console test record.

Validation: all 140 unit tests and 14 console cases pass on Java 25.
Checkstyle reports existing issues in untouched GUI and storage tests.
